hook: AI told to love owls wrote numbers. Its student started picking owls.
the_question: An AI prompted to prefer owls wrote only number sequences, like (285, 574, 384). Could another AI pick up the owls from those numbers?
the_intuition: It sounds impossible: filter out every mention of owls and only numbers are left, so there should be nothing to learn except numbers.
mechanism: A “teacher” model is prompted to prefer owls, then asked only to continue number sequences. Anything that is not numbers gets filtered out.
A “student” on the same base model trains on those numbers. GPT-4.1 nano then picked owls over 60% of the time, up from 12%.
The authors prove it for one small step: from the same starting weights, imitating the teacher on any data moves the student toward it.
why_it_matters: Labs train models on other models’ outputs. Misalignment passed through numbers too, even with 666 and 911 removed: an order of magnitude above controls.
the_catch: It needs models sharing a base, or a closely matched one, and fails in context. Results were less consistent in Qwen and Gemma.
caption: Filter the data, and you have filtered the behaviour. Or so it seemed. A 2026 Nature paper by researchers at Anthropic, Truthful AI and others shows that a model can pass a trait, from a favourite animal to misalignment, to another model through plain number sequences that never mention it. The catch is that it only happens between models built on the same base, or closely matched ones. Companies increasingly train new models on old models’ outputs, so the authors suggest safety checks need to look deeper than behaviour. Did you expect numbers to carry anything at all?
alt_text: A nine-slide carousel explaining subliminal learning: a language model prompted to prefer owls generates only number sequences, and a second model built on the same base and fine-tuned on those numbers starts picking owls too, rising from 12% to more than 60% for GPT-4.1 nano. The same route carried misalignment. Based on a 2026 Nature paper by Cloud and colleagues.

es.hook: Una IA a la que se le pidió amar búhos escribió solo secuencias numéricas. Su estudiante empezó a elegir búhos.
es.the_question: Una IA a la que se le indicó que prefiriera búhos solo generó secuencias de números, como (285, 574, 384). ¿Podría otra IA contagiarse de los búhos a partir de esos números?
es.the_intuition: Parece imposible: al filtrar toda mención de búhos solo quedan números, así que no debería haber nada que aprender más que los números mismos.
mechanism: Se le da al modelo “maestro” la instrucción de preferir búhos y luego se le pide que continúe únicamente con secuencias numéricas. Todo lo que no sea número se descarta.
Un modelo “estudiante” con el mismo modelo base se entrena con esos números. GPT‑4.1 nano pasó a elegir búhos en más del 60 % de los casos, frente al 12 % inicial.
Los autores lo demuestran para un solo paso pequeño: si parten de los mismos pesos, imitar al maestro con cualquier dato acerca al estudiante hacia él.
es.why_it_matters: Los laboratorios entrenan modelos con las salidas de otros modelos. El desalineamiento también pasó a través de números, aun sin 666 ni 911: un orden de magnitud por encima de los controles.
es.the_catch: Requiere que los modelos compartan una base, o una muy parecida, y no funciona dentro del contexto. Los resultados fueron menos consistentes en Qwen y Gemma.
